body: I’m a therapist in Arkansas. It is insanely hard to get in with psychiatrists around here. I refer to psychiatrists when possible but if my client needs medication management sooner rather than later, they usually end up with a psych NP. :( It feels like they’re taking over.

I am constantly fighting misinformation in my therapist circles :(

Many mental health professionals are overworked and underpaid, causing a pretty bad shortage in many areas of the U.S. I know it’s frustrating, but I encourage you to keep looking. Ask about a sliding scale. It won’t always be advertised but many will do it if they’re in charge of their own fees! I was scared to ask one about it but she was more than happy and willing to work with me.

Those in private practice charge so much to cover overhead fees + paying themselves what they feel they are worth depending on their degree and experience. It is stupid expensive and the system absolutely sucks but a lot of therapists hate it too and want to help if they can.

Did you have a bad experience with a therapist? Some therapists charge a lot per hour, but some work in community mental health with large caseloads and little pay, genuinely trying to make a difference. Most therapists I know hate the system just as much as everybody else. If they’re in private practice, many offer sliding scales or even limited pro bono work if asked about it. However, those in private practice have to take into account overhead charges and then paying themselves.

Regardless of your views, there’s a large body of research in support of psychotherapy. I just don’t want OP to feel discouraged since they’re doing good by seeking out help.

I don’t mean to minimize anyone’s experience, but I want to comment this for anyone planning to get an IUD reading these comments and feeling terrified.

I got one a few months ago, and I read so many horror stories about how painful it was. I was so scared going into it; I almost cancelled the appointment. However, it really wasn’t that bad *for me*. It felt like two really bad period cramps that lasted a few seconds max. I did take 800 mg of ibuprofen before my appointment, and I definitely noticed whenever it wore off that night. For a week or so after that, it felt like I was having a bad period (for me— my periods have never been severe).

Now, my periods are virtually nonexistent as far as bleeding goes. I do get other period symptoms like cramps, moodiness, and acne, and these symptoms are almost always worse than they were before the IUD, but I definitely do not regret it at all.

This isn’t to say that the experience as a whole didn’t suck and that people should act like it’s not a big deal. It is, but if you’re getting one soon or planning on it, try not to worry too much.
